In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of a hybrid material composed by thermotropic liquid crystal and carbon nanotubes.
the development and characterization of hybrid nanocomposites, based on thermotropic liquid crystal polymers (HBA PET), and single walled carbon nanotubes (SWCNTs).
the study of the self organization and of the photoinduced charge transport of single wall carbon nanocomposites.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the nanocomposites here investigated are characterized by a complex and intriguing morphology, that is the basis for a strong and efficient interaction between the components.

the nanocomposite is characterized by an effective electronic interaction at the interface polymer/nanotubes, which is triggered by the presence of the polymer fibers, and by a self-organization of the carbon nanotube in the LCP matrix.
a strong interfacial coupling between the two components of the nanocomposite has been demonstrated, with a possible use of the nanocomposites as a photoactive material.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the nanotubes are able to induce the alignment in the polymer matrix, and the polymer is able to induce the photoinduced charge transport in the nanotubes.

the nanotube bundles are aligned in the matrix and that the photoinduced charge is transferred from the polymer to the nanotube, which in turn can be considered as the first step for an effective use of the nanocomposite as an electronic material.

we have demonstrated the possibility of a controlled self-organization of SWCNT bundles in a LCP matrix, and the occurrence of an effective electronic interaction at the interface between the two phases, that could be exploited in future applications.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the hybrid material can be used as a platform for the development of new optoelectronic devices.
a hybrid material composed by SWCNT embedded in a LCP matrix could be used to produce new materials with enhanced electronic and photonic properties.
the hybrid system we have developed is an effective platform for the study of the interaction between carbon nanotubes and polymer matrix.
